knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
render_start = Sys.time()

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(EDI)
```

For a time-to-event outcome, the event time is often known only to lie in an
interval: a patient was still event-free when the study closed (right censoring), or
an infection was only found at the next scheduled visit (interval censoring). This
article shows how to record censored outcomes in EDI (Experimental Design and
Inference), analyze right- and interval-censored data, which inference classes accept
interval censoring, and what censoring assumes. It assumes you know the four steps
of an EDI analysis (design, assign, record responses, infer) from
[Get started](EDI.html).

## Recording censored outcomes

For a `"survival"` response, EDI records each outcome as an interval `(y_L, y_R]`
that the event time is known to lie in:

| What you know | Record it as |
|---|---|
| The event happened at time `t` | `y = t` |
| Event-free at last contact, time `t` (right censored) | `y_L = t, y_R = Inf` |
| The event happened before time `t` (left censored) | `y_L = 0, y_R = t` |
| The event happened between visits at `a` and `b` (interval censored) | `y_L = a, y_R = b` |

With `add_all_subject_responses()` you pass three vectors `ys`, `y_Ls` and `y_Rs`;
each subject has either a `ys` value or both bounds, and `NA` in the others.
`add_one_subject_response()` takes the same three arguments one subject at a time.
The [survival cookbook](cookbook-survival.html) is the full worked example for right
censoring, including the randomization test, bootstrap, `InferenceSuite` and a
sequential design; this article only adds what is different.

## Right censoring at the end of follow-up

In many trials censoring is administrative: patients enroll over two years, the
study closes at year three, and anyone still event-free is censored at however long
they have been followed.

```{r right-censored}
set.seed(2)
n = 150
X_surv = data.frame(age = round(rnorm(n, 60, 10)), stage = sample(1:3, n, replace = TRUE))
des_rc = DesignFixediBCRD$new(n = n, response_type = "survival", verbose = FALSE)
des_rc$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(X_surv)
des_rc$assign_w_to_all_subjects()
w_rc = des_rc$get_w()

event_time = rexp(n, rate = exp(-1 - 0.5 * w_rc + 0.02 * (X_surv$age - 60) +
                                0.3 * (X_surv$stage - 2)))
follow_up = 3 - runif(n, 0, 2)          # enrolled during years 0-2, study ends at year 3
observed = event_time <= follow_up

des_rc$add_all_subject_responses(
  ys   = ifelse(observed, event_time, NA),
  y_Ls = ifelse(observed, NA, follow_up),
  y_Rs = ifelse(observed, NA, Inf)
)
table(event_observed = observed)

inf_rc = InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr$new(des_rc, verbose = FALSE)
inf_rc$num_cores = 1L
log_hr = inf_rc$compute_estimate()
ci_rc = inf_rc$compute_lik_ratio_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)
exp(c(hazard_ratio = log_hr, ci_rc))
```

The true hazard ratio is `r round(exp(-0.5), 2)`; the estimate is
`r round(exp(log_hr), 2)`, and the interval contains the truth. Every survival class in
EDI accepts right-censored data.

## Interval censoring: events found at scheduled visits

Now suppose the event (say, a recurrence) can only be detected at clinic visits every
three months, for two years. A recurrence found at the month-9 visit happened
sometime after month 6. A recurrence found at the first visit happened sometime
before month 3, which is left censoring, the case `y_L = 0`. Patients with no
recurrence by month 24 are right censored there.

```{r interval-censored}
set.seed(7)
n = 120
X_ic = data.frame(age = round(rnorm(n, 60, 10)))
des_ic = DesignFixediBCRD$new(n = n, response_type = "survival", verbose = FALSE)
des_ic$add_all_subjects_to_experiment(X_ic)
des_ic$assign_w_to_all_subjects()
w_ic = des_ic$get_w()

# Weibull event times; treatment multiplies the time scale by exp(0.4), about 1.5
t_event = rweibull(n, shape = 1.5, scale = 12 * exp(0.4 * w_ic - 0.02 * (X_ic$age - 60)))
visits = seq(3, 24, by = 3)
y_L = sapply(t_event, function(t) max(c(0, visits[visits < t])))
y_R = sapply(t_event, function(t) if (t > max(visits)) Inf else min(visits[visits >= t]))

des_ic$add_all_subject_responses(y_Ls = y_L, y_Rs = y_R)
table(type = ifelse(is.infinite(y_R), "right censored",
                    ifelse(y_L == 0, "left censored", "interval censored")))
head(cbind(y_L, y_R))
```

No subject has an exact time, and you should not invent one (the visit time or the
midpoint), because that biases the analysis. Instead, use a class that takes the
intervals as they are. A Weibull accelerated-failure-time model gives a time ratio:

```{r ic-weibull}
inf_wb = InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE)
inf_wb$num_cores = 1L
exp(c(time_ratio = inf_wb$compute_estimate(),
      inf_wb$compute_lik_ratio_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)))
```

On interval-censored data, the Cox class switches to the semiparametric
proportional-hazards model of
[icenReg](https://cran.r-project.org/package=icenReg) (`ic_sp()`), and the log-rank
class to the interval-censored log-rank test of Sun (1996), via
[interval](https://cran.r-project.org/package=interval):

```{r ic-cox-logrank}
inf_cox = InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE)
inf_cox$num_cores = 1L
exp(c(hazard_ratio = inf_cox$compute_estimate(),
      inf_cox$compute_asymp_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)))

inf_lr = InferenceSurvivalLogRank$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE)
inf_lr$num_cores = 1L
inf_lr$compute_asymp_two_sided_pval()
inf_lr$set_seed(1)
inf_lr$compute_rand_two_sided_pval(r = 200, show_progress = FALSE)
```

For these Weibull data with shape 1.5, a time ratio of $e^{0.4} \approx 1.49$ is the
same as a hazard ratio of $e^{-0.4 \times 1.5} \approx 0.55$, so the two models agree.
The randomization test needs nothing new: it redraws `w` from the design and
recomputes the interval-censored statistic. A test of a nonzero null time ratio
$e^{\delta}$ (`delta` in `compute_rand_two_sided_pval()`) rescales the treated
subjects' interval bounds by $e^{\delta}$ as it rescales exact times (a bound of 0 or
`Inf` stays put), so the Weibull class's randomization confidence interval for the
time ratio, `inf_wb$compute_rand_confidence_interval()`, works on interval-censored
data too.

### Median and restricted mean survival differences

A hazard ratio or time ratio leans on a model. Two classes compare the arms without
one, on the time scale itself: the difference in median survival
(`InferenceSurvivalKMDiff`) and the difference in restricted mean survival time, the
area under each arm's survival curve up to a horizon $\tau$
(`InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff`). On interval-censored data both read the
survival curves from the Turnbull NPMLE instead of Kaplan-Meier.

```{r ic-km-rmst}
inf_km = InferenceSurvivalKMDiff$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE)
inf_km$num_cores = 1L
inf_km$set_seed(1)
km_est = inf_km$compute_estimate()
km_ci = inf_km$compute_asymp_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)
inf_km$set_seed(1)
km_p = inf_km$compute_rand_two_sided_pval(r = 200, show_progress = FALSE)
c(median_difference = km_est, km_ci, rand_pval = km_p)

# tau = 24 months, the planned follow-up, fixed in the protocol before the data are seen
inf_rmst = InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE, tau = 24)
inf_rmst$num_cores = 1L
inf_rmst$set_seed(1)
rmst_est = inf_rmst$compute_estimate()
rmst_ci = inf_rmst$compute_asymp_confidence_interval(alpha = 0.05)
inf_rmst$set_seed(1)
rmst_p = inf_rmst$compute_rand_two_sided_pval(r = 200, show_progress = FALSE)
c(rmst_difference = rmst_est, rmst_ci, rand_pval = rmst_p)
```

The treated arm's median recurrence time is `r km_est` months later, and over the
first 24 months treated patients are recurrence-free for `r round(rmst_est, 2)` months
longer on average (95% interval `r round(rmst_ci[1], 2)` to `r round(rmst_ci[2], 2)`).
The median difference is a multiple of three months: the Turnbull curve only drops
between visits, so its median sits on the visit grid. That makes the median a coarse
statistic, and its interval is wide; here it covers zero although the randomization
test rejects at the 5% level. The restricted mean uses the whole curve and is more
precise.

Neither class has a closed-form standard error on interval-censored data, so
`compute_asymp_confidence_interval()` is really a nonparametric bootstrap interval,
at the bootstrap defaults: B = 501, a percentile interval for the median difference
and a BCa interval for the restricted mean. It is reproducible after `set_seed()`,
but each call refits the Turnbull NPMLE about a thousand times and takes seconds
rather than milliseconds. BCa needs B of at least 501; if time matters more than the
BCa correction, call `compute_bootstrap_confidence_interval(B = 199, type = "percentile")`
yourself. Other differences from right-censored data:

- **The Bayesian bootstrap is refused**, with an error, because the Turnbull fit
  (`interval::icfit()`) takes no weights. Use the ordinary bootstrap.
- **The jackknife of a median is unreliable**: `InferenceSurvivalKMDiff`'s
  jackknife-Wald interval and p-value are usually `NA`, with a warning.
- **Randomization confidence intervals are not available** for either class (their
  units do not fit the randomization interval search); the randomization p-value is.
- **A median may not be reached.** If an arm's survival curve never falls to 0.5,
  for example at an early interim look, the median difference is `NA`. The restricted
  mean is defined however short the follow-up, so use it then.

Why prespecify `tau`? By default the horizon is the smaller of the two arms' last
finite visit times, here also 24 months. That default depends on the data: a few
missed final visits in one arm would shorten it and change what is being estimated.
EDI fixes the horizon once, from the observed data or from your `tau`, and holds it
fixed in every randomization and bootstrap draw. (Recomputing it in each draw would
make the null draws compare restricted means over different horizons and can take
away almost all the test's power.) Choosing `tau` in the protocol, typically the
planned follow-up, makes the estimand known before the data are seen.

## Which classes accept interval censoring

A class that cannot use left- or interval-censored data refuses at construction, with
an error that says so, rather than treating the intervals as right-censored. Trying
each class on this design shows which ones accept it:

```{r ic-classes}
survival_classes = c("InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr", "InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr",
                     "InferenceSurvivalLogRank", "InferenceSurvivalGehanWilcox",
                     "InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff", "InferenceSurvivalKMDiff",
                     "InferenceSurvivalStratCoxPHRegr", "InferenceSurvivalDepCensTransformRegr")
accepts = sapply(survival_classes, function(cl)
  tryCatch({ get(cl)$new(des_ic, verbose = FALSE); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE))
data.frame(accepts_interval_censoring = accepts)
```

In short:

- **Accept left- and interval-censored data:**
  [`InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalCoxPHRegr.html)
  (icenReg semiparametric PH),
  [`InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalWeibullRegr.html)
  (the interval-censored Weibull likelihood),
  [`InferenceSurvivalLogRank`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalLogRank.html) and
  [`InferenceSurvivalGehanWilcox`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalGehanWilcox.html)
  (interval-censored rank tests),
  [`InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalRestrictedMeanDiff.html)
  and [`InferenceSurvivalKMDiff`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalKMDiff.html) (survival
  curves from the Turnbull NPMLE
  [(Turnbull 1976, doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1976.tb01597.x)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1976.tb01597.x);
  their intervals come from the bootstrap, see
  [above](#median-and-restricted-mean-survival-differences)).
- **Exact and right-censored data only:** the stratified Cox, dependent-censoring,
  frailty and KK matched-pair survival classes.

Not every procedure is available on the interval-censored path; for example, the
Bayesian bootstrap is not. Each class's help page lists what changes. The `InferenceSuite`
(see the [survival cookbook](cookbook-survival.html#everything-at-once)) skips the
classes that do not apply.

## What censoring assumes

All of these methods assume censoring is *noninformative*: given the covariates, a
patient censored at time `t` has the same future risk as one still under follow-up.
Administrative censoring at the end of the study satisfies this; dropout because a
patient felt worse does not. In a randomized trial the comparison stays fair as long
as censoring does not depend on prognosis differently in the two arms, but that is an
assumption, not something the data can confirm.
[`InferenceSurvivalDepCensTransformRegr`](../reference/InferenceSurvivalDepCensTransformRegr.html)
relaxes it under a parametric model (a bivariate log-normal for event and censoring
times), for right-censored data.
